newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends firmer on foreign fund inflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends firmer on foreign fund inflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday amid an influx of foreign funds for the rallying stock market, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.520, off an intraday high of T$27.515, against Tuesday's T$27.525 close.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$201.5 million.
Dealers said foreign funds worth some US$30-40 million emerged in late trade, pushing the Taiwan dollar higher.
The inflows nevertheless werre not enough to push the local currency outside of its recent narrow trading band.
"The Taiwan dollar rise was mostly offset by U.S. dollar buying, which was reflecting the strong U.S. dollar overseas," said one dealer.
Dealers said they noted keen interest by importers to buy U.S. dollars when the rising Taiwan dollar neared T$27.50 level, thus further checking the local dollar's appreciation.
For Thursday, a T$27.50-27.54 range was seen.
